title: Exports since 4.6.1 suddenly include 4.8 MB of ICU data
body:
### Tested versions

4.6.1 compared against 4.6, but unexplained size increases were found in 4.6.2, 4.7, 4.8.dev3, 4.8.dev5, 4.8.dev6 likely for the same reason

### System information

Irrelevant as this was run on Github actions

### Issue description

Follow-up to #123468 which I closed.

After I migrated [my project](https://github.com/MewPurPur/GodSVG) to Godot 4.6.1, I suddenly noticed a very sharp increase in executable size. My assets are very lightweight, probably totaling less than 2 MB, and I use aggressive size optimizations, so I noticed this immediately, but I'm not good with buildsystem stuff, so I thought it would soon be fixed and kept my project on 4.6 for a while. When I tried to migrate to 4.8.dev5, I was surprised to see the ZIPs were still way bigger, even after I used the new available optimizations.

I've only reproduced this on my project with 4.6 vs 4.6.1 web exports and quite specific buildsystem options, but ZIPs for other versions and platforms have also bloated up way more than expected, so they might have this problem too.

I ran the following workflow file on Github actions:

```yml
name: compare-godot-pck

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

env:
  GODOT_GOOD_VERSION: 4.6-stable
  GODOT_REGRESSED_VERSION: 4.6.1-stable

jobs:
  build-good:
    name: Good PCK export
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout GodSVG
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          path: godsvg

      - name: Set up Godot Editor
        run: |
          mkdir -p ~/godot-editor
          cd ~/godot-editor
          wget -q https://github.com/godotengine/godot-builds/releases/download/${GODOT_GOOD_VERSION}/Godot_v${GODOT_GOOD_VERSION}_linux.x86_64.zip
          unzip Godot_v${GODOT_GOOD_VERSION}_linux.x86_64.zip
          mv Godot_v${GODOT_GOOD_VERSION}_linux.x86_64 ~/godot-editor/godot
          echo "~/godot-editor" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      - name: Export project
        run: |
          cd godsvg
          mkdir -p build/web
          godot --headless --export-pack "Web" build/web/normal.pck

      - name: Upload PCK
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: godsvg-${{ env.GODOT_GOOD_VERSION }}-pck
          path: godsvg/build/web/normal.pck

  build-regressed:
    name: Regressed PCK export
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout GodSVG
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          path: godsvg

      - name: Set up Godot Editor
        run: |
          mkdir -p ~/godot-editor
          cd ~/godot-editor
          wget -q https://github.com/godotengine/godot-builds/releases/download/${GODOT_REGRESSED_VERSION}/Godot_v${GODOT_REGRESSED_VERSION}_linux.x86_64.zip
          unzip Godot_v${GODOT_REGRESSED_VERSION}_linux.x86_64.zip
          mv Godot_v${GODOT_REGRESSED_VERSION}_linux.x86_64 ~/godot-editor/godot
          echo "~/godot-editor" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      - name: Export project
        run: |
          cd godsvg
          mkdir -p build/web
          godot --headless --export-pack "Web" build/web/bloated.pck

      - name: Upload PCK
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: godsvg-${{ env.GODOT_REGRESSED_VERSION }}-pck
          path: godsvg/build/web/bloated.pck
```

One PCK was 2.67 MB, the other was more than double the size at 5.42 MB. I put them in a folder and added the following script to it:

```py
import struct

def read_pck(filename):
    with open(filename, "rb") as f:
        f.seek(32)
        f.seek(struct.unpack("<Q", f.read(8))[0])
        files = []

        for _ in range(struct.unpack("<I", f.read(4))[0]):
            path_len = struct.unpack("<I", f.read(4))[0]
            path = f.read(path_len).decode()
            f.seek(8, 1)
            size = struct.unpack("<Q", f.read(8))[0]
            f.seek(20, 1)
            files.append((size, path))

        return files

for filename in ["normal.pck", "bloated.pck"]:
    files = read_pck(filename)
    print(f"\n{filename}: {len(files)} files")

    for size, path in sorted(files, reverse=True)[:5]:
        print(f"{size:12,} {path}")
```

I used the documented PCK file structure to read the PCK directory directly, count the files, and print the five largest entries in each PCK. Running the script with `python3` gave me this:

```
normal.pck: 852 files
   1,196,875 .godot/imported/DroidSansFallback.woff2-dc4d9bb62ed0af22bad408ae21580e72.fontdata
     187,461 .godot/imported/NotoSans-ExtraBold.woff2-afe5c7a9b5b0881b2a4600b03512ba6b.fontdata
     187,425 .godot/imported/NotoSans-SemiBold.woff2-146a883351ad06e51ad735a7586f2309.fontdata
      59,338 translations/uk.po
      59,029 translations/ru.po

bloated.pck: 853 files
   4,797,072 icudt_godot.dat
   1,196,875 .godot/imported/DroidSansFallback.woff2-dc4d9bb62ed0af22bad408ae21580e72.fontdata
     187,461 .godot/imported/NotoSans-ExtraBold.woff2-afe5c7a9b5b0881b2a4600b03512ba6b.fontdata
     187,425 .godot/imported/NotoSans-SemiBold.woff2-146a883351ad06e51ad735a7586f2309.fontdata
      59,338 translations/uk.po
```

In a nutshell, this means that since 4.6.1, there's an `icudt_godot.dat` file that's larger than the entire rest of my project. I'm not aware of anything in my project being improved by the addition of this file.

I couldn't isolate the exact point where this happened, but the quite laconic #115827 seems like the most likely cause.
